Subject: Access controls & support access — post-discovery follow-up

Thanks again for the call today, Tim — really appreciated the level of detail from the FinTrust security team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary concerns: PII handling, retention windows, and detailed audit logging for any support / break-glass access.
- Desired controls: role-based access control (RBAC) with least-privilege roles, time-bound privileged sessions, MFA for break-glass, and immutable audit trails.
- Residency requirement: FinTrust prefers US-only residency for customer data but may require EU for a subset of clients.

Questions you asked for concrete answers on (we'll bring details in the tech deep-dive):
1) How Redwood enforces RBAC across Console/API and how roles map to token scopes.
2) How support access is performed (jumpbox vs ephemeral sessions) and what the approval/audit workflow looks like.
3) Break-glass procedures: who can trigger it, emergency authorization flow, and the logging/notification model.
4) Data residency and retention configurable per-tenant.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev to run a 60-min tech deep-dive next week focused on RBAC, support access controls, and logging. (Dev: can you be available?)
- I'll share our RBAC overview and SOC 2 summary immediately after this thread.
- We'll produce a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones for a pilot + security review.

Available slots: Wed 3/4 10:00–11:30 PT, Thu 3/5 14:00–16:00 PT. Let me know what works and if you prefer an EU-specific session for residency questions.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side before the tech deep-dive:

1) Residency: For our pilot we need US-only, but we're evaluating a future product line that will require EU residency. Can you confirm whether residency can be enforced at the tenant level and whether logs/indices can be pinned to region?

2) Support access / break-glass: We need a documented emergency process that includes:
   - explicit approvers (>=2 people)
   - time-limited sessions with automatic revocation
   - real-time notification to our on-call and a tamper-evident audit trail that records commands and session transcripts

3) RBAC: We'd like to see a mapping of Redwood roles to least-privilege scopes (read-only, redacted-PII-read, admin, support-ephemeral). Also how API keys and service tokens are rotated and scoped.

4) Deliverables: Please provide SOC 2 type II summary, the RBAC one-pager, and a short description of your support access workflow prior to the deep-dive so our security folks can pre-read.

If possible, can we lock Wed 3/4 10:00 PT for the deep-dive? Dev, Laura — hope you can join.

Best,

Timothy — great, booked for Wed 3/4 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Attaching the items you requested so your security team can review before the call.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-rbac-overview.pdf — RBAC model, role mappings, and token/scopes guidance (summary page + examples).
- redwood-support-access-process.pdf — support access playbook: ephemeral sessions, approval flow, notification channels, and logging retention.
- soc2-audit-summary.pdf — SOC 2 Type II summary and scope (controls relevant to data handling and access).

Quick answers to the residency / logging items you raised:
- Residency: Yes — we support tenant-level data residency. For hosted Redwood, data and logs for a tenant can be pinned to a region (US, EU). We'll bring the exact region-to-storage flow to the call.
- Break-glass: Our standard flow requires a 2-person approval for emergency access; sessions are ephemeral and recorded to an immutable audit log. Session transcripts and actions are retained per tenant retention policy and surfaced in Console.
- Audit trails: All support sessions and admin actions generate tamper-evident audit events (SHA256 chain), with exportable logs. Retention windows are configurable per-tenant; default is 365 days.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: Share MAP draft and HubSpot deal link (done).
- Dev: Prepare a short demo of RBAC role creation + an example break-glass flow that shows audit events.
- FinTrust: Share any specific retention/PDL numbers if you want non-default settings for the pilot.

If you want me to send the MAP ahead of the call, I can — fine to iterate during the pilot planning.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
